title: Tenant-scoped retry buckets and audit-linked deprovision for SCIM provisioning
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Our SCIM pipeline currently retries failed user/group provision/deprovision events globally which causes noisy retries, cross-tenant cascading failures, and makes audit traces hard to correlate. We lack tenant-scoped retry budgets and an auditable linkage between provisioning attempts and the final deprovision action. This ticket implements a tenant-scoped retry budget system, attaches a stable audit token to each logical SCIM operation (create/update/delete), and ensures deprovision outcomes are recorded with an audit-linked tombstone. Goals: (1) limit retry amplification per tenant, (2) provide deterministic idempotency keys and checksums to avoid duplicate work across retries, (3) surface audit-linked traces for every eventual deprovision so security/compliance teams can reconcile, (4) create safe-mode kill-switch to pause destructive operations at tenant scope.
acceptance_criteria: Each SCIM logical operation emitted by our ingest layer carries an immutable audit_token (UUID) persisted in the operation store
Retry budget is enforced per-tenant with configurable daily/quota windows; retries beyond budget are moved to a tenant-specific DLQ
Deprovision operations attach the audit_token and a tombstone record that is queryable via the audit log UI
Idempotency: applying an operation with the same audit_token and checksum is a no-op; duplicates are detectable and deduplicated at the executor node
Observed provisioning success rate for tenants with transient failures improves (retries trimmed) and platform CPU usage on retry paths reduces by >=25% in 2-week canary
Runbook exists with steps to manually reconcile DLQ entries and re-enable tenant safe-mode; runbook linked from incident page
Security review completed and KMS-approved audit_token storage format (encrypted at rest)
design_notes: High-level design: introduce a small immutable metadata header on every SCIM event: {audit_token, tenant_id, op_type, checksum, origin_ts}. The ingest service assigns the audit_token and computes a lightweight checksum across canonicalized payload. Retry controller tracks per-tenant counters with a token-bucket style budget (quota window configurable by tenant). When retries exceed budget, events are moved to a tenant DLQ with a tombstone that references the audit_token. Executor nodes consult the operation store for audit_token before executing: if a completed marker exists for that token, the execution is a no-op. For deprovision flows, the executor writes both the action outcome and an audit-tombstone entry atomically in the operation store. System exposes an endpoint to pause destructive ops for a tenant (safe-mode) which flips a tenant flag and transitions active queues to DLQ. Observability: trace-id = audit_token to correlate traces across services. All writes of audit_token are encrypted using KMS and logged to the audit log stream with redaction rules for PII.
implementation_steps: schema: extend SCIM event header in ingest (audit_token:string, checksum:string)
ingest: compute checksum (canonical JSON -> SHA256) and assign audit_token
retry-controller: implement tenant token-bucket with Redis-backed counters and fallback window
executor: consult operation-store before applying; implement atomic write for tombstone + outcome
DLQ: create tenant-scoped DLQ queues and admin APIs to list/replay/ack
console: add audit-token search in Audit Log UI and tenant safe-mode toggle
security: encrypt audit_token and checksum at rest with KMS; add retention and TTL policies
tests: unit + integration + fault-injection canary in staging; enable rollout flag for 10 tenants
migration_plan: Phase 1: Ingest assigns audit_token and checksum but keeps legacy retry path enabled; executor ignores audit_token. Phase 2: Gradual rollout of retry-controller and executor dedupe on feature-flagged tenants (start with non-production and 10 small customers). Phase 3: Flip default flag and stream DLQ + tombstone data to long-term audit store. Phase 4: Deprecate legacy global retry path after 6 weeks of monitoring and manual reconciliation. Detailed timelines: week 1-2 feature flags and canary, week 3-4 tenant rollouts, week 5 lock default, week 6 deprecation and cleanup.
rollback_plan: Feature flags at ingest and executor allow quick rollback. To undo: flip ingest flag to stop emitting audit_tokens (safe but leaves existing tokens in store), disable retry-controller to revert to global retries, requeue DLQ entries back to global retry queue if necessary. All actions reversible via console by platform ops. Post-rollback, run audit to find operations emitted during window and reconcile tombstones.
monitoring_metrics: audit.search.latency - latency of audit-token lookup in console
system.cpu.retry-path - CPU on retry-controller and executor retry code paths
